research-sampling-steps.alt: Left: a population of 48 people drawn as dots in three colors (three kinds of people, such as age groups). Random sampling gives every member the same chance of being chosen; 12 are chosen, 4 of each color, so the sample mirrors the population. It decides who is studied and lets results generalize to the population. Middle: the sample of 12. Right: random assignment uses chance to split the 12 into a treatment group and a control group of 6 each. It decides which condition each person gets and lets an experiment claim cause and effect. A study can use either step, both, or neither.
